The old Hag, had realised a while ago, that being everywhere, was tedious. That being present all the time, monotonous. He had decided, that things needed to change. So he had sought out the Community Market, in the forest of brotherhood.

There in the forest, he found what he was looking for. The Thorac. Could a more perfect caravan guard, have ever been created. A desire to see the world before they died, strong warriors, and one can sleep, whilst the other drives. So the Hag sought them out, and made them an offer, that they would never refuse.

The Saen of the market, were able to grow him caravans, out of Carrion vine. Living caravans, how useful! With his new enterprise swinging into action, the Hag, sent out his first trade caravan. To the Great Roost and the Central Market. Like a vine climbing a wall, his trade roots began to spread, to feel out the nooks, and take hold in the crannies. A vine to syphon off the nectar of others, and grow beautiful flowers of its own.

His caravans spread out to the Holnareem, bringing supplies and trade, to isolated pockets. They sought out the live ships of the Seafairers, and eked out a path to the tree of life. All driven by his Thorac, all guided by the Hag. Wherever communities of Gaea, should create goods, the Hag would seek them out. A harmless old Shryke, a friend to all.

An old Hag, with his Thorac caravan guards, approached the citadel of Arsenal. The Arsenal. A great city of the Deva. There he would seek out the Grand Magistrate, and offer his humble wares as trade. A grand city such as this, would have need.
I'm sure the Hag will come knocking, the spectrus are favoured by Zille.

As the caravan approaches the mountain, a horn blows . It resonates through the wastes around it, and the banners flutter in the chill wind. It is cold here, too cold for comfort. The caravan comes close to the massive stone gates, and they swing wide, souldning of stone grating on stone like the opening of a granite coffin. A guide beckons with all four hands. The caravan rolls inside and the gates are pulled closed with a dull thud. Deep into the mountain they go, up or down they do not know. A street system, carved into the rock itself. Countless side alleys and chasms branching off from the main arteries that connect the people in Arsenal. To a great hall, one of many, they go. The caravan is halted and they disembark. Walking, walking more. Through the chasms and ravines. Some paved, some not. Shortcuts, the guide said. Like a giant spiderweb. Finally they come to a tower reaching up into the heavens. Climbing, climbing some more. It feels like hours. Finally they come to the to of the tower. Thick plumes of smoke bellow from the caldera formed behind them formed from the countless chimneys fired to unimaginable temperatures. Seated in a chair behind the desk is the Magistrate, hands folded. Her eyes gleam like gold. "What is it that you seek?"

The Hag was impressed, everywhere he looked, such craftsmanship. These beings, they created things from stone and metal, that rivalled what the Saen grew from nature. A wise and noble looking race, what terrors must they hide. 'Oh great and wise Magistrate, I am but a humble an old trader. Throughout the lands there are whispers, whispers of a great city, the Arsenal. I have journeyed far, to look upon your magnificence. If it would please you, I would like to establish trade with your noble people. Allow me to procure, that which is not abundant here, for you great Magistrar. I have need of armour, of a very precise specification, armour that has no reflection, and cannot be mirrored.'

"We shall be pleased to trade with you. We are of need of raw materials, mainly ore. You shall be useful. Now, an armor, unreflective. I think I have just the thing. Follow." With that, she descended into the bowels of the mountain once more, and the Hag followed. Soon they came to a massive armory, racks and racks of all manners of weapons and armor lined the walls and sat upon the floor like boulders. The Magistrate came to a rack of near-black sets of armor. "These are made of cast iron. Nigh-indestructible and completely unreflective. They, however, are quite heavy and hard to produce. What have you to trade one for?"

"The weight won't be a problem, but my buyers are very discerning. They are looking for an armour, that will render the wearer immune from being copied. There are many eyes watching, if you understand my meaning. My buyers wish to be protected from their master." Said the Hag, as he closely examined the armour. "My buyers are prepared to wait if your craftsman require time to work on the problem". The Hag scratched his head, then looked thoughtful for a minute. "I can acquire a very rare metal, a metal that is abundant in the deep, but not on Gaea."

Making small food units seem regular: how larger table size reduces calories to be consumed

People with bad spacial reasoning probably tend to eat more food anyway. If you can't objectively determine the quantity of food that you are consuming, you probably struggle with many things in life, including over-eating.

The same concept has been known for ages - use smaller plates, and you'll put less food on them. That's much more pleasant than staring at a half unfilled plate, which is obviously just based on feefees but it's still quite effective if you're trying to get a grip on portion control.

In the 1950's the average plate size was 8 inches. Today it's 12 inches. If you use today's 'salad' plates for dinner instead, which are actually the proper 50's size, you will find yourself suddenly serving appropriate portion sizes.
